answer: Price identity issuance by congestion, not a flat fee. Each epoch only a few slots open, and the marginal price climbs convexly as a single funding source mints more — so a farm pays a total rising faster than head count, never N times a cheap floor, with the price reaching its zenith under bulk demand. One honest agent mints at the low first-slot price, a steady ember of cost; a bulk minter cannot echo that cheap rate across heads, since each extra fake costs more than the last. Convex marginal pricing makes mass creation self-taxing.
